fixture.scope: Diagnostic fixed-batch publication timings, metadata growth and compaction intervention.
fixture.methodology: One evolving private fixture, fixed prequeued batches, fresh direct worker per batch. 512-MiB/one-CPU PostgreSQL and 2-GiB/one-CPU engine with 1536-MB query limit, swap disabled, INSERT grouping and 16-MiB row groups. Target autovacuum disabled to isolate file growth; native VACUUM is the explicit intervention. Split BEGIN/apply/COMMIT adds round trips; SQL wrappers write unlogged diagnostic rows. Apply-operation elapsed times are nested within worker apply time and must not be summed with it. Resource observers run outside worker wall timing but their CPU is included in cgroup deltas. Source queueing, observer/catalog reads and compaction are outside publication timings. One trace spans the fixture with excluded per-window completion witnesses. This diagnoses growth and intervention; it is not an offered-load capacity or isolated CPU-saving comparison.

fixture.scope: Bounded direct mixed load with the existing native autovacuum on a shorter interval.
fixture.methodology: Fresh private volumes and identical cached PostgreSQL/core/pgduck/storage images in every mode. Both paths use the same text-valued events and current apply_change_run functions. One warmup transaction (one seed row per table) is published before measurement; it is excluded from publication counts and object traces. Direct worker persists across all measured transactions and uses bounded 1-second/32-transaction coalescing and uses a loopback superuser. Journal uses the existing managed supervisor, unprivileged worker, source schema validation and protocol streaming; a test-only next_batch wrapper caps publications at 1 for the matched control or 32 for the coalesced reference. Original journal admission, publication, generation fencing and recovery functions remain unchanged. This compares the implementations, not just the isolated cost of journal durability: worker lifecycle, privileges, metadata checks and protocol differ. Coalesced reference uses a 1-second interval and INSERT grouping. Two-second resource/progress observers are identical; CPU includes observer processes in database/engine containers, excludes host/controller/MinIO. Publication delay is a sampled upper bound. No competing local qualification, no cache clearing, no production capacity or significance claim. This cohort uses one CPU/512 MiB for PostgreSQL and one CPU/2 GiB for pgduck (1536-MB engine query limit). Postgres-user observers read database/engine process memory; a separate root observer adds the root-owned direct worker without requiring ptrace capabilities. All modes run both observers. Worker exit diagnostics record its lifetime RSS peak and CPU, including warmup. memory.peak includes fixture startup and page cache; it is not process RSS. Sustained phase has paced mixed transactions; memory phase has one large INSERT transaction and no offered pacing. Memory payloads use per-row MD5 strings with varied blocks. Samples are every two seconds and can miss short peaks; cgroup lifetime peak and worker VmHWM supplement samples. Expanded profile disables swap; both RAM and swap limits are recorded. Logical decoding work memory is 64 KiB in both modes, so larger transactions stream without the immediate debug setting. No concurrent qualification runs. This fixture configures native pg_lake autovacuum through private ALTER SYSTEM settings and reloads its existing worker. The release and deployment defaults are unchanged. File counts are sampled with progress and can miss brief peaks. Maintenance CPU, WAL and S3 operations are inside measurement; source/mirror verification is afterward.

conclusions: Row apply dominates commit; fixed-batch UPDATE/DELETE cost grows with current data-file count.
Native result scans load and FOR UPDATE-lock all current data-file metadata before pruning, once per mutation.
Compaction preserves exact rows/checkpoint and reduces the observed apply cost.
Skipping unused stats in the position-delete receiver did not materially improve this copy-on-write workload; no production patch was promoted.
Internal SPI helpers disable normal query tracking. Explicit diagnostic-only native counters expose the catalog query/decode costs.
A 20-second native autovacuum pilot deadlocked with publication; the one-shot worker exited. This is a failed maintenance qualification, not a throughput improvement.
next_required_work: Add bounded whole-transaction deadlock recovery or coordinate maintenance at publication boundaries, then repeat offered-load qualification.
caveats: Elapsed timings are diagnostic, not CPU or production-capacity estimates.
Function, catalog and SQL timings are nested; do not sum overlapping layers.
One evolving fixture per mode; no cold-cache isolation or statistical significance claim.
Native instrumentation and the negative native candidate are separate experimental images; the pinned vendor tree and release prerequisite patchset are unchanged.
The failed maintenance pilot does not qualify automatic replay/supervision or establish a stable production rate.
